newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez sells property portfolio, predicts profit.
newsitem.headline: Suez sells property portfolio, predicts profit.

text.p: Venerable French holding company Cie de Suez said Monday it would earn a profit in 1996, ending two years of huge losses due to bad property investments.

Suez Chairman Gerard Mestrallet said the company would earn a 1996 consolidated profit of about 800 million francs ($145 million) after exceptional charges of 3 billion francs ($545 million) on property and other investments.

"I can confirm our return to profit in 1996," Mestrallet told reporters, adding that he expected a 25 percent rise in the group's 1996 pre-tax profit before one-time items. He said he expected that result to climb again this year.

He also announced the sale of a property loan portfolio worth about 4 billion francs ($737 million) to real estate fund Whitehall Street Real Estate Limited Partnership VII, run by U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs.

Mestrallet said the sale, for about 3 billion francs ($545 million) or 30 percent of the property's original value on the company's books, would result in a charge in 1996 of about 1 billion francs ($181 million).
Mestrallet was upbeat at a news conference called to announce the profit forecast, highlighting what he called a profound change in the company's strategy and financial situation during 1996.
The key events leading to that change were the sale of investment banking arm Banque Indosuez and the taking of a majority stake in Belgian utility Tractebel.
